00 / A NOTE TO THE READERTHE MAKING OF A MIND

I am still
becoming.

I have never thought of life as a straight line toward a single achievement. It is a collection of questions, encounters, failures, discoveries, and small decisions that slowly shape the way a person sees the world.

I am drawn to different forms of creation: music that communicates without explanation, images that preserve a moment, and technology that can turn an idea into something useful. At first, these interests may seem unrelated. To me, they share one purpose: to understand, create, and contribute.

This is not a finished story. It is an archive of the experiences and people that continue to shape the person I am becoming.

“A meaningful life is not measured only by what we achieve, but also by what we choose to make better.”
CHAPTER 01 / WHERE QUESTIONS BEGAN

Some chapters
change the way
we see the world.

Growing up, I learned that life does not always follow the plans we imagine. Losing my father during the COVID-19 pandemic, when I was twelve, became one of the experiences that changed how I understood time, responsibility, and the people around me.

As I continued school, I also learned to carry responsibilities while exploring what I could become. I took on opportunities as a Mandarin tutor, photographer, translator, model, and occasional event host. Each role taught me something different: patience, communication, discipline, independence, and the courage to keep learning.

The shoreline in this photograph reminds me that a person can hold both uncertainty and possibility at once. The past cannot be rewritten, but it can become part of the reason we move forward with greater intention.

“I want my experiences to become direction, not limitation.”
02 / THE PEOPLE BESIDE MESHARED JOURNEY · SHARED PURPOSE
FIG. 02 — THE PEOPLE WHO STAY
MORE THAN A SUPPORT SYSTEM

No journey
is built alone.

Behind every milestone is a circle of people who make the journey possible. The people in this photograph represent more than shared memories. They are part of the team that has accompanied me through different seasons of life — encouraging me to keep going, exchanging ideas, and helping me find solutions when challenges appear.

Achievements may carry one person's name, but the process is rarely individual. There are conversations behind an idea, patience behind a practice, and people who offer perspective when the next step is not yet clear.

I have come to value collaboration not simply as a way to divide tasks, but as a way to see a problem from more than one point of view. Together, we learn, create, and celebrate progress that none of us would have reached in exactly the same way alone.

A TRIBUTE TO THE PEOPLE WHO MAKE THE PROCESS MEANINGFUL.
03 / ANOTHER LANGUAGEMUSIC · VIOLIN
A PASSION THAT TAUGHT ME TO LISTEN

Finding my
own resonance.

Music has been one of the most personal ways I have learned to express myself. The violin asks for patience: progress comes from returning to the same passage, listening carefully, and accepting that small improvements matter. It has taught me discipline, sensitivity, and how to communicate emotion without needing words.

Performing with orchestras has also shown me the beauty of listening as a group. Every musician carries an individual part, but the music only comes together when each person pays attention to the others.

04 / A WIDER PERSPECTIVEOBSERVATIONS FROM NATURE
THE WORLD IS NOT A BACKDROP

Learning to
look closer.

Nature has a way of making me pause. It reminds me that the world is a connected system: water, soil, energy, living things, and human activity constantly influence one another. A change in one part can affect everything around it.

That perspective shapes the questions I bring into science and engineering. I do not want to see technology as something separate from nature. I want to understand how it can work with natural systems, reduce harm, use resources more thoughtfully, and help communities live better.

Being in nature also gives me room to think. It makes complexity feel less intimidating and reminds me that meaningful solutions often begin with careful observation.

“We do not inherit the Earth from our ancestors; we borrow it from our children.”— A widely shared environmental proverb
05 / IDEAS INTO ACTIONSCIENCE · ENGINEERING · IMPACT

Curiosity
with a purpose.

My interest in engineering comes from a simple question: how can we use what we know to respond to problems people experience every day?

01 / WATER

HYDROSORT

Simulasi dan pelajari lebih dalam ↗

A high-school prototype exploring floating river-waste collection and small-scale hydropower. The project taught me to test ideas against real conditions, understand the limits of a prototype, and think about environmental problems as connected systems.

02 / MATERIALS

BIMASSTIC

An exploration of bioplastic made from domestic and agricultural organic waste. Through repeated experiments, I learned how formulation, processing, and material properties interact — and why careful iteration matters.

03 / DIRECTION

ENGINEERING FOR TOMORROW

I am interested in the intersection of energy, materials, water, and environmental infrastructure. My long-term ambition is to build technology and products that address practical challenges while respecting the systems that sustain life.
